biography.plain_text: Prince Mohammed bin Salman is Saudi Arabia's crown prince and prime minister. A law graduate who moved through advisory and ministerial roles, he was appointed crown prince in 2017. His public programme centres on Vision 2030, while the Misk Foundation he established supports Saudi youth through education, entrepreneurship, culture and leadership development.

long_biography.plain_text:
Prince Mohammed bin Salman earned a law degree at King Saud University before beginning public service as a government adviser. He worked with the Riyadh governor and at the royal court before becoming defence minister. His appointment as crown prince in 2017 placed him next in line to King Salman, and he later became prime minister.

His defining domestic programme is Vision 2030, which links economic diversification with government reform and new cultural, tourism and technology sectors. Through his economic council and chairmanship of PIF, he directs key parts of its implementation. He also established the Misk Foundation, giving youth education, entrepreneurship and creative development a continuing place alongside the state-led transformation agenda.
